uncited: Texture Packing and Atlas Organization consolidates multiple volumetric data sources or semantic channels into fewer, larger texture resources to optimize memory bandwidth, reduce state changes, and emulate 3D texture support in constrained environments [S1, unofficial].

It differs from [3D Texture Storage and Sampling](3064-3d-texture-storage-and-sampling.md) by focusing on the logical arrangement of data within the resource rather than the hardware storage format, and from [Sparse Volume Texture (SVT)](7011-sparse-volume-texture-svt.md) by keeping data dense and resident rather than sparse and paged.
The family shares the goal of reducing the number of active texture units and state transitions by grouping data.
The core mechanism involves mapping logical data indices (whether semantic channels, discrete volumes, or spatial slices) into a single physical texture coordinate space.
This requires a deterministic mapping function in the shader to reconstruct the logical coordinate from the physical one.
The method assumes the target hardware supports the resulting texture format (e.g., 3D textures, 2D arrays, or multi-channel 2D textures).
The techniques originate from general graphics optimization practices to reduce driver overhead and memory bandwidth usage.
Multi-channel packing is common in procedural generation [S1, unofficial]. 3D atlas packing is used in animation and multi-dataset visualization [S1, unofficial].
Image texture atlas packing was developed to enable volume rendering in WebGL 1.0 environments where `Texturing3D` is unsupported [S1].
The metadata-based skip method addresses gaps in residency-based skipping by optimizing resident empty space [S1, unofficial].
